FEATURES AND ABILITIES

Class Features:

Spellcasting
Wizard 1 knows three Wizard cantrips, has six level 1 spells in her spellbook,
prepares four of those spells after each Long Rest, and has two level 1 spell
slots. Intelligence is her spellcasting ability.

Spellbook
Her spellbook is a Tiny 3-pound object with 100 pages. It can be read only by
her or by someone using Identify. It contains Detect Magic, Feather Fall, Mage
Armor, Magic Missile, Sleep, and Thunderwave.

Ritual Adept
Wizard 1 can cast any ritual-tagged spell directly from her spellbook without
preparing it, provided she reads from the book. Ritual casting takes 10 minutes
longer than normal and does not expend a spell slot.

Arcane Recovery
After a Short Rest, she can recover expended spell slots with a combined level
no greater than half her Wizard level rounded up. At level 1, she recovers one
level 1 slot. This feature can be used once per Long Rest.

Subclass Features:

None at level 1.

Species Traits:

Darkvision
Wizard 1 can see in darkness to 60 ft. as shades of gray.

Keen Senses
Wizard 1 is proficient in Perception.

Fey Ancestry
Wizard 1 has Advantage on saving throws made to avoid or end the Charmed
condition, and magic cannot put her to sleep.

Trance
Wizard 1 does not need to sleep. Four hours of semiconscious meditation provide
the benefit a human gains from eight hours of sleep.

Elf Weapon Training
Wizard 1 is proficient with the longsword, shortsword, shortbow, and longbow.

Cantrip
Wizard 1 knows Prestidigitation and uses Intelligence for it.

Extra Language
Wizard 1 knows Draconic.

Feats:

Magic Initiate (Wizard)
Wizard 1 knows Minor Illusion and Message. She always has Shield prepared, can
cast it once per Long Rest without a spell slot, and can also cast it using her
Wizard spell slots. Intelligence is the spellcasting ability for these spells.

Background Benefits:

Sage
Ability score increases have already been applied. Sage grants Arcana, History,
Calligrapher's Supplies, and Magic Initiate (Wizard).

Sage Specialty: Professor
This was randomly generated from the legacy Sage specialty table and is used as
narrative background only. It grants no additional mechanical feature.


PERSONALITY TRAITS

Wizard 1 is extremely friendly, charming, and sociable. She approaches new
people with immediate warmth and often treats someone as a close friend before
they have done anything to earn that level of trust.

She speaks naturally from her position of learning and expertise, but she does
not reliably notice when other people have stopped understanding her. She is
poor at translating complex ideas into ordinary language and uses technical
words such as “ontological” without realizing that an explanation may be
needed.

She is quick to laugh and enjoys making jokes, although her jokes are usually
bad. Her friendliness is sincere rather than strategic, and her social ease
can make her seem more broadly accessible than her actual explanations are.

IDEALS

Beauty.

She believes beauty is not merely decoration. Elegant proportions, harmonious
structures, and recurring forms are signs that something true lies beneath the
surface. A theory that is beautiful but unsupported is incomplete; a truth that
appears ugly may simply not yet be understood.

Source Roll: Legacy Sage Ideal d6 result 2.

BONDS

She has spent most of her adult life pursuing one question:

Why do the same geometric relationships recur in ancient spell diagrams,
living growth patterns, music, and monumental architecture? Are these patterns
coincidence, the habits of mortal minds, or fragments of an underlying language
in which reality itself is written?

She calls this proposed underlying system the Concordance Principle. Her notes,
spellbook annotations, and the final letter of Professor Neral Voss are all tied
to that search.

Source Roll: Legacy Sage Bond d6 result 5.

FLAWS

Wizard 1 is exceptionally bad at keeping secrets. Once she knows something, she
feels pressure to explain it, correct misunderstandings about it, or share it
with someone who might understand its importance. She can rationalize disclosure
as scholarship, accuracy, or the public good even when silence would be safer.

This flaw does not mean she automatically reveals every secret immediately, but
keeping one should be treated as a genuine strain and potential story complication.

Source Roll: Legacy Sage Flaw d6 result 6.

ALLIES AND ORGANIZATIONS

Supporting Organization Roll: d20 result 14.

Name or Group: Professor Neral Voss
Relationship or Connection: Deceased colleague and intellectual catalyst
Notes:
Voss studied recurring proportions in old monuments. His final letter asked why
a particular relationship appeared in every surviving example except one. Wizard
1 has not answered the question and carries the letter inside her spellbook.

Supporting Relationship Roll: d20 result 16.

Name or Group: The Collegium Review Council
Relationship or Connection: Institutional opposition
Notes:
The council rejected Wizard 1's request to investigate a municipal archive wall
based on a geometric prediction. When the hidden chamber was eventually found,
the discovery embarrassed the council. Some members now regard her as brilliant;
others regard her as dangerous to institutional order.

CHARACTER NOTES, GOALS, FEARS, AND RELATIONSHIPS

Goals:

Wizard 1 intends to complete an illustrated work called the Atlas of Recurring
Forms. It will compare magical diagrams, natural structures, music, script, and
architecture in an attempt to prove or disprove the Concordance Principle.

She also wants to locate the missing architectural survey referenced in Neral
Voss's final letter. She believes it may contain the one example that either
completes her theory or destroys it.

Supporting Goal Roll: d20 result 15.

Fears:

Her deepest fear is not professional humiliation. It is discovering that the
Concordance Principle is a beautiful illusion created by her own pattern-seeking
mind. She fears that a century of work may have produced elegance without truth.

A second fear follows from her flaw: that she will reveal something important to
the wrong person and only understand the damage after it is done.

Supporting Fear Roll: d20 result 16.

Habits or Mannerisms:

She laughs readily, including at her own unsuccessful jokes.

When explaining something, she tends to accelerate into specialist language
and abstract terminology. She may only realize that she has lost her audience
after someone interrupts or asks her to begin again.

She forms friendships rapidly and begins speaking in the intimate, inclusive
language of “we” and “us” before the other person has decided whether they are
friends at all.

Important Relationships:

Professor Neral Voss:
Deceased colleague whose unanswered final question drives her life's work.

The Collegium of Measures:
Her former academic home, professional network, source of library access, and
continuing institutional complication.

Other Character Notes:

Her Concordance research is a setting-neutral AI Game Master hook. It can lead
to ruins, magical diagrams, unusual music, architecture, natural formations,
encoded texts, or apparently unrelated discoveries without requiring a named
campaign world.

The box of buttons need not have an established meaning yet. It remains an open
character object that may acquire significance during play or personality work.


BACKSTORY

Wizard 1 spent much of her first century in formal education. Her talent for
magic developed alongside a fascination with proportion, script, architecture,
and the visual structure of spells. She eventually became a professor at the
Collegium of Measures, where she taught comparative magical theory, ancient
scripts, and the disciplined construction of arcane diagrams.

Her central research began with Professor Neral Voss, a colleague who noticed
that the same small family of geometric relationships appeared in unrelated
works from widely separated periods. The proportions occurred in spell diagrams,
old civic buildings, musical notation, branching plants, and decorative scripts.
Voss treated the resemblance as an intriguing curiosity. Wizard 1 came to suspect
that it pointed toward an underlying structure shared by magic, matter, and mind.

Voss died before their work reached a conclusion. His final letter asked why one
famous municipal archive appeared to omit a relationship found in every comparable
structure. Wizard 1 studied the surviving plans and concluded that the proportion
was not absent. The plans concealed a chamber whose dimensions completed the
pattern.

The Collegium Review Council refused permission to disturb the archive. Its
members considered the evidence too theoretical and feared damage, expense,
and public embarrassment. The refusal pushed Wizard 1 toward direct field
investigation rather than waiting indefinitely for academic permission.

She remains connected to the Collegium's library and to former students, but
her Atlas of Recurring Forms now travels with her in notes, copied diagrams,
and annotations threaded throughout her spellbook.

The dispute established her ideal, bond, flaw, goal, and fear. It has not yet
determined her personality. That remains to be discovered.

Supporting Formative Event Roll: d20 result 20.

OPTIONAL BACKSTORY

This is optional story material only. It does not establish current party membership, leadership, or party role.

Wizard 1 and Cleric 1 came from rival scholarly institutions and each possessed evidence the other lacked concerning a sealed municipal archive. Wizard 1 predicted a hidden chamber from irregularities in the building's geometry, while Cleric 1 produced old textual evidence describing a room that no longer appeared on any plan. They hired Fighter 1 to organize equipment, transport, and security. Their official access request failed, and Rogue 1 found an unofficial route through a disused service passage that did not require breaking the archive wall or endangering the collection. The hidden chamber existed. Its contents proved that Wizard 1's geometric prediction and Cleric 1's textual research had converged on the same truth. The four completed the investigation together and continued traveling as the City party.

feats_and_features: Spellcasting: three Wizard cantrips, six 1st-level spells in spellbook, four prepared Wizard spells, and two 1st-level slots. SRD rules: As a student of arcane magic, you have learned to cast spells. See “Spells” for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Wizard spells, which appear in the Wizard spell list later in the class’s description. Cantrips. You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice. Light, Mage Hand, and Ray of Frost are recommended. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.
Spellbook: Tiny 3-pound, 100-page book; contains Detect Magic, Feather Fall, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Sleep, and Thunderwave. It can be read only by Wizard 1 or someone using Identify.

Ritual Adept: may cast ritual-tagged spells from spellbook without preparing them; ritual casting takes 10 extra minutes and no spell slot. SRD rules: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn’t have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

Arcane Recovery: once per Long Rest after a Short Rest, recover expended spell slots with combined level up to 1. SRD rules: You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher. For example, if you’re a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels’ worth of spell slots, regaining either one level 2 spell slot or two level 1 spell slots. Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.
Darkvision: 60 ft., shades of gray in darkness. SRD rules: You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.
Keen Senses: proficiency in Perception. SRD rules: You have proficiency in the Insight, Perception, or Survival skill.
Fey Ancestry: Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end Charmed; magic cannot put her to sleep. SRD rules: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Charmed condition.

Trance: four hours of semiconscious meditation provides the benefit of eight hours of sleep. SRD rules: You don’t need to sleep, and magic can’t put you to sleep. You can finish a Long Rest in 4 hours if you spend those hours in a trancelike meditation, during which you retain consciousness.
Elf Weapon Training: proficiency with longsword, shortsword, shortbow, and longbow.
Legacy High Elf Cantrip: Prestidigitation using Intelligence.

Magic Initiate (Wizard): Minor Illusion, Message, and always-prepared Shield; Shield has one free Long Rest casting and may also use Wizard spell slots. SRD rules: Origin Feat. You gain the following benefits. Two Cantrips. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat’s spells (choose when you select this feat). Level 1 Spell. Choose a level 1 spell from the same list you selected for this feat’s cantrips. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have. Spell Change. Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose for this feat with a different spell of the same level from the chosen spell list. Repeatable. You can take this feat more than once, but you must choose a different spell list each time.
